A Low frequency respiratory signal is modulated to higher frequencies by chopper circuits and then amplified by amplifiers. The proposed CMOS signal processing system is implemented by 0.18μm technology and simulated with cadence environment. The switching frequencies of both the choppers and SC filters are 1 KHz, while gains of DDA and two-stage amplifier are 78.28 dB and 72.52 dB respectively. The overall gain of the signal processing system is 40.62 dB while other simulated results are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Optimization of LFC controller of two area system integrated with wind energy using HSA
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Incorporation of wind energy into power systems has gathered substantial momentum globally due to its abundant supply and environmental benefits. Despite its numerous benefits, wind power in grid integration poses many challenges. The non-dispatchable and inherent intermittent qualities of wind energy not only insert additional fluctuations to the existing frequency deviation, they also reduce frequency stability by decreasing the regulation capability and the inertia. This paper presents the significance of these effects, which causes a larger frequency deviation in the proposed system. In this paper optimization algorithm used to optimize PID controller is Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA). The simulation and analytical results represented here provide guidance on calculating maximum wind power penetration level using frequency deviation limit.

articleTitle: Development of algorithm for soil moisture retrieval using palsar data for bare soil
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: An algorithm was developed using existing empirical model for determining soil moisture content of bare soil. Phased array L-Band synthetic aperture radar (PALSAR) data was first classified for different land cover such that; water, urban, tall vegetation, short vegetation and bare soil. The objective was to determine the soil pixel from study area by masking the other class. An inversion technique based on empirical model was derived and applied on bare soil pixel to determine the soil moisture. Finally a Graphical User Interface (GUI) was developed to retrieve soil moisture for bare soil area along with the classified map of the study area.

articleTitle: Design of photonic crystal fiber with negative chromatic dispersion and low confinement loss
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: A design of photonic crystal fiber (PCF) with large improved negative dispersion and low confinement loss is discussed in this paper. The effect of different design parameters, such like non uniform air hole structures and pitch on the effective refractive index and the total dispersion and confinement losses are investigated. It can also be observed that the proposed non uniform air holes cladding structure provides very low chromatic dispersion as well as flattened chromatic dispersion in the communication wavelength range from 0.9 to 2.0 μm.

articleTitle: Evaluation of state probabilities based on deterministic criterion for a distribution system with distributed generation employing boot strapping technique
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: This paper describes an algorithm for evaluating state probabilities of a distribution system having distributed generation. The probabilities have been classified as healthy, marginal and risky state probabilities based on a deterministic criterion which is based on load and capacity available. Uncertainties in the capacity available from substation and that from distributed generation have been considered. Uncertainties have been considered in two stages i.e. one stage considered the operable availability and the second stage considers random variations around the rated capacity available that of substation or distributed generation. To evaluate the state probabilities boot strapping has been incorporated in Monte Carlo simulation so as to enhance computational efficiency. The algorithm has been implemented on a sample distribution system incorporating annual load duration curve.

articleTitle: Despeckling of SAR images using discrete shearlet transform
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: In this paper, a new SAR image despeckling method is presented. Discrete shearlet transform based on multiresolution analysis is used to obtain the transformed coefficients. Shearlet transform is good in processing multidimensional data, and have the property of high directional sensitivity and optimal sparse representation. Shearlet coefficients of noise free image are modeled using two sided generalized Gamma distribution (GrD) because of heavy tailed distribution of clean image transformed coefficients and the speckle noise is modeled using zero mean Gaussian distribution. The distribution parameters are estimated using method of log cumulants (MoLC). A Bayesian MAP estimator is used to estimate the noise free shearlet coefficients. The performance of the proposed method and some other existing methods are evaluated and compared using parameters peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR) and equivalent number of looks (ENL). Results are taken on synthetic image as well as real SAR image. The obtained results show the dominance of proposed technique over other existing techniques.

articleTitle: Design of single and dual band pass filter using substrate integrated waveguide with DGS
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Defected ground structure (DGS) is introduced on top side of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) Resonator. Due to this DGS, SIW Resonator resonate two different frequencies with one Transmission zero between two pass bands. Both resonant frequencies and transmission zero can be controlled by changing the position of DGS. For filter design Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 with substrate height of 0.508mm & copper thickness of 17um has been used.

articleTitle: Temperature based performance analysis of doping-less tunnel field effect transistor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Recently, the doping-less Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (TFET) has emerged as a novel device for the replacement of conventional TFET due to its similar trend in current characteristics and reduced fabrication complexity with low cost. However, the impact of temperature on its performance is yet an undiscovered aspect. The semiconductor devices are known to have significant temperature dependence characteristics. Thus, it is very much of importance to analyse the behavior of the device at different temperature. In this concern, an extensive study has been performed for temperature sensitivity analysis of the behavior of the doping-less TFET. For this, transfer characteristics, energy band diagram and carrier concentration are considered as DC figure of merits, whereas Transconductance (gm), gate-to-drain capacitance (Cgd)), cut off frequency (fT) and gain bandwidth product (GBW) are used as RF performance parameters. Further, the effect of variation in temperature on the Off-state and its components such as Band to Band Tunneling (BTBT), Trap Assisted Tunneling (TAT) and Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) is also analyzed with different drainchannel spacer widths for doping-less TFET. All the simulations have been performed on Silvaco ATLAS simulator.

articleTitle: TrustRBAC: Trust role based access control model in multi-domain cloud environments
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Cloud computing is one of the most leading paradigms in information technology. It offers various cost-effective information technology services over the internet. To keep each entity secure and privileged, a secure and efficient access control is essential. However, trust and access control are the fundamental security concepts of storing, delivering and protecting cloud computing resources and services. This, the concepts of role-based access control mechanism and trust management are combined with cloud computing environment. In this paper, TrustRBAC a novel role-based access control model based on trust management is proposed for single and multi-domain cloud environment. The model calculates the direct trust and recommendation trust with security policies for both domains. Further, the performance analyses show that the proposed model is suitable for cloud environment which can improve efficiency and reliability of the system.

articleTitle: Controlling ambipolar behavior and improving radio frequency performance of hetero junction double gate TFET by dual work-function, hetero gate dielectric, gate underlap: Assessment and optimization
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: In this paper, investigation for different configurations of N-type Hetero Junction Double Gate Tunnel Field-Effect Transistor (HJ-TFET) with Dual metal gate work function and hetero gate dielectric material along with gate underlap is performed to achieve improvements in DC and analog/RF performances. In this regard, the creation of hetero-junction using band gap engineering maintains the lower energy band and higher energy band at source/channel and drain/channel interface respectively to provide high ON current and low ambipolar behavior. A high-density layer of N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> type concentration is added at source/channel junction to obtain abruptness at the same. Further, application of work function engineering on the gate electrode over the channel specified as Tunnel gate (M1) towards the source region and Auxiliary gate (M2) towards the drain region facilitates to achieve higher ON-state current at the cost of poor analog/RF responses. In this concern, hetero gate dielectric and gate under-lap concepts are implied to reduce parasitic capacitances which enhance RF performance of the device. Furthermore, optimization of work function for tunnel gate and the auxiliary gate has been performed to assess the optimum values of work function.

articleTitle: Cluster statistics based normalization for online fault diagnosis of self-powered neutron detectors
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Self Powered Neutron Detector (SPND) is a widely used sensor for measuring neutron flux in a nuclear reactor. In this work we propose a novel cluster statistics based normalization scheme to normalize SPND measurements. These normalized measurements are subsequently used in a recursive Principal Component Analysis (PCA) based approach for detecting faults and identifying faulty SPNDs in an online manner. The motivation behind cluster statistics based normalization is that faults effect only individual sensors, while simultaneous variations in multiple sensors are usually caused by dynamic variations in the reactor operation. The proposed normalization approach is applied on SPND data obtained from an operating nuclear reactor and results compared with existing sensor statistics based normalization approach. The results demonstrate the utility of the proposed normalization approach.

articleTitle: Kluster: Application of k-means clustering to multidimensional GEO-spatial data
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: There have been several developments both in hardware and softwares for capturing and processing geographic information. The results yield by the processing of geo-spatial data helps for efficient planning and strategic decision making. Due to the amount of geo-spatial data captured and stored every day, it has become of utmost importance that the data be processed and the results be delivered in time. With the increasing amount of data, application of distributed and parallel frameworks which have been proven capable of processing large amounts of data in other domains has become necessary. These frameworks have to be extended to support geo-spatial data and related geo-processing operations. In this paper, we have extended the regular k-means clustering to support processing of multi spectral geo-spatial raster data over Hadoop. By performing clustering on multiple dimensions (multiple spectrums) simultaneously over a distributed processing framework, Apache Hadoop, our approach allows detailed clustering. Our approach in addition to considering n-dimensional data also allows processing it by utilizing heterogeneous and distributed resources for faster processing and delivery results.

articleTitle: Issues of concern in storage system of IoT based big data
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Internet of Things is now a day's popular due to promote of society, but IoT generate bountiful data and it require high processing speed for process & storages. During the analysis of literature It has been observed the issues related to storing & processing of voluminous heterogeneous data. Internet of Things applications generate bountiful heterogeneous data & distributed computing is one of the approach which can solve this problem. Acquisition, Management, Processing and Mining areas of IoT Big data, with other associated technicalities were defined. The proposed paper Initially analyzes the present research work moreover, the challenges and opportunities associated with IoT big data research are identified. Further the paper discuses existing functional Framework of Cloud-Based IOT Application.

Author Keywords: Storage as a Service of Cloud Computing

articleTitle: Multiobjective optimization of 2DOF controller using NSGA-II for shell and tube heat exchanger
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: In this paper, multi-objective optimization of two degree of freedom (2DOF) controller using Non-dominated Sorting of Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II) for the problem of shell and tube heat exchanger system is considered. The objective functions are deployed considering, set point tracking and disturbance rejections for the shell and tube heat exchanger system. The pareto set of solution for conflicting objective functions set point tracking and disturbance rejections are obtained after optimizing simultaneously all the five parameters of 2DOF controller. The result obtained using genetic algorithm of multi-objective optimization is compared with single objective optimization method. MATLAB software tool is used to verify above strategy.

articleTitle: Impact of time-bandwidth product on cooperative spectrum sensing over AWGN and fading channels
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Cognitive radio (CR) plays a key role in upcoming 5-G wireless technology. The main task of CR technology is to detect the presence of licensed user or primary user (PU) for effective utilization of the spectrum. In this paper, fist we study the non-cooperative spectrum sensing with a variation in time-bandwidth product over a non-fading (additive white Gaussian noise, AWGN) channel and fading channels (Rayleigh and Rician). Analytical and simulation frameworks are presented over fading and non-fading channels. Second, we consider voting rule for hard decision combining in cooperative spectrum sensing and the impact of time-bandwidth product over an AWGN and fading channels is investigated. An optimal decision fusion rule is investigated with respect to time-bandwidth product that minimizes the total sensing error in cognitive radio network.

articleTitle: Uncertain cloud resource provisioning using the predictive approach
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Cloud computing is a sort of Internet-based figuring that gives shared PC handling resource and information to PCs and different gadgets on request. It is a model for empowering omnipresent, on-request access to a common pool of configurable registering resource (e.g., computer networks, servers, stockpiling, applications and servers, storage, applications and services), which can be quickly provisioned and discharged with negligible administration exertion. Cloud computing may be a virtualized surroundings which gives administrations similarly as Virtual machine (VM) instances. These VM instances are dissimilar. Cloud clients might pick which setup alternately sum about instances they need, Concerning illustration there would numerous resources available. There might make a few circumstances which prompt underutilization about these resources. So, a proper resource allocation technique has to be done to increase the revenue of the cloud provided. Resource Provisioning means the selection, deployment, and run-time management of software (e.g., database server management systems, load balancers) and hardware resources (e.g., CPU, storage, and network) for ensuring guaranteed performance for applications. Resource Provisioning is an important and challenging problem in the large-scale distributed systems such as Cloud computing environments.

articleTitle: Robust decentralized fast output sampling technique via reduced order models based power system stabilizer for multimachine power system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Power System Stabilizers (PSSs) are added to excitation systems to enhance the damping during low frequency oscillations. In this paper, the design of decentralized PSSs for 10 machines with 39 buses using fast output sampling feedback via reduced order model is proposed. In multi-machine power system the order of the states matrix is very large. The main objectives of order reduction is to design a controller of lower order which can effectively control the original high order system so that the overall system is of lower order and easy to understand. The state space matrices of the reduced order system are chosen such that the dominant eigenvalues of the full order system are unchanged. The other system parameters are chosen using the PSO with objective function to minimize the mean squared errors between the outputs of the full order system and the outputs of the reduced order model when the inputs are unit step. Design of fast output sampling feedback controllers via reduced order model using PSO method is proposed for good damping enhancement for various operating points of multi-machine power systems. This paper also presents a comparatively study of design of fast output sampling feedback controllers via reduced order model using Particle PSO method, and Davison method technique for multi-machine system. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) order reduction method based fast output sampling feedback controller gives very good results, less complexity and also economic in designing of PSSs comparatively Davison method and balance truncation technique.

articleTitle: A novel proposed deer algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Information, Communication, Instrumentation and Control (ICICIC)
abstract: Deer is a social animal though it is wild animal. Its behaviour is to be in groups. Many activities are done in groups. There is specific pattern in the activities performed by the deer. It was felt that these activities can be modeled and used to obtain solution of non linear problems. The social activities of deer to form as group motivated us to propose algorithm, called Deer Algorithm. (DA). This proposed Deer algorithm shares many features of the Genetic Algorithms (GA). In this paper we are performing clustering is unsupervised classification on newly proposed algorithms Deer algorithm for the reproduction activity of Deer. Deer algorithms is based on the optimization of some objective function (fitness function). Experimental results are compared with the evolutionary-based clustering algorithm and swarm based clustering algorithms such as PSO, GA, FA, BA. It is shown that the proposed algorithm can achieve the optimal number of clusters and, in most cases, outperforms the other methods on several benchmark datasets in terms of intra cluster and inter cluster distances, robustness, convergence speed and accuracy.
